name: Forecast liquidity and monitor the 10-day liquidity coverage ratio (daily)
summary: Each business day the liquidity team in Total Fund Management forecasts the fund's cash needs and checks that it holds enough liquid assets to meet them under stress. Analysts load and reconcile opening cash, collect capital calls, closings, distributions, margin, plan transfers and debt maturities from several teams and systems, and associates update a spreadsheet forecast, value the unencumbered liquidity buffer and compute the 10-day liquidity coverage ratio against its Board limit of 1.0x. A principal reviews the result, and shortfalls trigger calls to the funding and balancing teams. The work is slowed by re-keying inputs that arrive by email, waiting for deal teams to confirm closing dates and for the morning margin summary, and private fund call timing makes the forecast uncertain.

baseline.org_archetype: A national pension fund manager of about C$540 billion with C$122 billion of recourse leverage, C$54 billion of unfunded private commitments and weekly plan cash flows.
baseline.notes: Liquidity management moved into Total Fund Management in September 2020; the team is the Balancing, liquidity and collateral (treasury) team in the organisation file. Forecast models are spreadsheets fed by the investment book of record and private investments system.

trigger: Reconciled positions and custodian cash for the prior day are available, together with new margin, capital call, closing, distribution and plan transfer information.
end_state: The reviewed forecast and coverage ratios are published to the balancing, leverage, funding and Risk teams, loaded for Risk's limit monitoring and archived, with any funding actions agreed.

volume.seasonality: One forecast per business day. Effort rises in volatile markets with large margin flows (March 2020), at quarter ends when capital calls cluster, and around large closings and plan transfer dates.

evidence.note: Daily monitoring of liquidity risk; trading days per month from the calendar.

steps.name: Load overnight cash, positions and settled flows
steps.description: A scheduled job loads the prior day's reconciled positions, custodian cash balances by currency and account, settled trades and settled private cash movements from the investment book of record into the liquidity model's data tables.

error.defect_description: A late custodian file or an unbooked private wire leaves an account balance missing or wrong.

evidence.note: Overnight load of positions and cash into a forecasting model is common treasury practice. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large fund treasury team.

steps.name: Check opening cash balances
steps.description: The analyst compares opening cash by currency and account in the model with custodian portal balances and the reconciled position record, and checks that yesterday's expected flows actually settled. Differences above a small tolerance are listed as breaks.

error.defect_description: A small break is accepted that later turns out to be an unbooked margin payment.

control.basis: Daily cash reconciliation before cash balances are used for funding decisions

evidence.note: Daily reconciliation of cash positions is part of cash forecasting practice. Break rate and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Chase cash breaks with operations
steps.description: The analyst emails the reconciliation or settlements team with each unexplained difference, for example a failed FX settlement or a capital call paid but not booked, and waits for the explanation or correction before using the balance.

evidence.note: Common dependency of treasury on reconciliation teams. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large fund treasury team.

steps.name: Collect private market cash flows
steps.description: The analyst pulls capital call notices received and not yet paid, expected distributions, scheduled closings and loan drawdowns from the private investments administration system and the deal pipeline, and reads emails from deal teams about closings that have moved.

error.defect_description: A closing that slipped or a call due in a different currency is carried on the wrong date or in the wrong currency.

evidence.note: Private call and distribution timing is uncertain and notices carry estimates later reconciled. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Collect plan transfers, debt and hedge settlements
steps.description: The analyst adds the weekly net plan contribution transfer and the monthly benefit outflow requirement, commercial paper maturities and coupons, term debt maturities and FX forward settlements due in the forecast horizon, taken from the funding team's schedule and the book of record.

error.defect_description: A maturity or transfer date is entered a week late.

evidence.note: Weekly net plan cash flows and monthly net outflow requirements; payment obligations include debt repayments. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Pull the morning margin summary
steps.description: The analyst takes the collateral team's morning summary of margin paid and received, collateral posted, excess collateral held and expected initial margin changes, and adds expected variation margin from yesterday's market moves.

evidence.note: Collateral and margin are payment obligations; margin must be met within one or two days. Wait for the summary is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Compare yesterday's forecast with actual cash
steps.description: The associate lines up yesterday's forecast for today against actual opening cash and explains the largest misses, for example a capital call paid early or a distribution that did not arrive. Repeated misses lead to adjusted assumptions for that flow type.

evidence.note: Variance review against actuals is a standard forecasting step; the AFP article lists reviewing output. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large fund treasury team.

steps.name: Update the cash forecast model
steps.description: The associate enters or refreshes each flow by date and currency in the forecast spreadsheet for the next 10 business days, three months and beyond, applying probability weights to uncertain capital calls and distributions. Most inputs arrive by email or report and are re-keyed.

error.defect_description: A flow is entered with the wrong sign, date or currency, or double counted.

evidence.note: Spreadsheet receipts-and-disbursements forecasting with uncertain private flows. Shares and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Confirm large pending flows with deal teams
steps.description: For closings, drawdowns or calls above a size threshold that are not yet confirmed, the associate asks the deal team or funds operations for the expected date and amount and waits for replies, chasing by chat if a closing is within a few days.

next.condition: replies received or best estimate kept

evidence.note: Deal teams own closing timing; confirmation by email is common. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large fund treasury team.

steps.name: Calculate unencumbered liquid assets
steps.description: The associate takes positions in government bonds, money market securities and listed equities, removes securities already pledged as collateral or lent, and applies haircuts for stressed sale or repo values to arrive at the liquidity buffer by currency.

error.defect_description: Securities already pledged are counted as free, overstating the buffer.

evidence.note: Buffers are high-quality assets and funding sources; limit counts unrestricted eligible coverage assets. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Compute the 10-day liquidity coverage ratio and stressed coverage
steps.description: The associate divides the liquidity buffer by stressed outflows over the next 10 days, including stressed margin calls, capital calls, plan transfers, debt maturities and commercial paper that may not roll, and repeats the test at longer horizons. The results are compared with the 1.0x limit, internal early-warning levels and the 22% liquidity target.

error.defect_description: A stress assumption is left at an outdated level after a market move.

control.basis: Board-approved liquidity risk limit: 10-day liquidity coverage ratio minimum of 1.0x in the Integrated Risk Policy

evidence.note: 10-day LCR calibrated to stressed outflows, limit 1.0x, 2.9x at March 31, 2022; liquidity 23% versus 22% target. Steps and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Review the forecast and coverage ratios
steps.description: The liquidity principal checks the largest flows, the variance note, the buffer and the ratios against yesterday and market conditions, challenges probability weights on uncertain calls, and decides whether a shortfall or early-warning breach needs action today.

control.basis: Four-eyes review of the daily liquidity forecast before it is published

evidence.note: Review by a principal is assumed from the team structure. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large fund treasury team.

steps.name: Agree funding or cash-raising actions
steps.description: The liquidity principal works out how to cover the gap: issue or extend commercial paper, add repo against government bonds, use excess collateral, delay discretionary purchases or ask the balancing team to raise cash from the Balancing Portfolio, and calls the funding and balancing teams.

evidence.note: Liquidity is raised through commercial paper, term debt, repo, credit facilities and liquid assets; Big Eight used equity-collateral cash raising and term repo in March 2020. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Confirm commercial paper and repo capacity
steps.description: The funding principal checks outstanding commercial paper against programme capacity, dealer demand and pricing in each currency, and available repo lines, then replies with what can be raised by which date.

next.condition: large gap or ratio near floor

evidence.note: US commercial paper became unavailable to some funds in March 2020; funding capacity must be confirmed, not assumed. Shares and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Approve contingency actions and inform the CIO and Risk
steps.description: A TFM director approves larger actions such as drawing a credit facility, raising cash from the Balancing Portfolio or pausing discretionary commitments, and informs the CIO and Risk, which may lead to a remediation plan.

control.basis: Liquidity contingency and escalation procedures under the Integrated Risk Policy

evidence.note: Escalation procedures sit in the Risk Policy; TFM manages liquidity. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Publish the daily liquidity report
steps.description: The associate sends the forecast, the coverage ratios, liquidity as a share of net assets and any agreed actions to the balancing, leverage and funding teams, TFM leadership and Risk, and saves the version in the shared folder.

evidence.note: LCR and liquidity ratio are reported to Risk and governance. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Load ratios to the risk platform
steps.description: The analyst uploads the day's coverage ratio, buffer and stressed outflows to the risk platform so that Risk can monitor the liquidity limit independently and include it in its daily limit report.

error.defect_description: An upload fails silently or loads the prior day's file.

next.condition: large unexpected flow during the day

evidence.note: Risk independently measures and monitors compliance with all limits. Manual upload is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Archive the forecast and update the accuracy log
steps.description: The analyst saves the published forecast, logs forecast against actual for the main flow types and notes any manual assumptions used, so tomorrow's variance check and monthly accuracy reviews have a record.

evidence.note: Record-keeping step assumed. Times and probabilities are the author's estimates for a large fund treasury team.

steps.name: Reforecast after a large intraday flow
steps.description: When a large unexpected margin call, an accelerated capital call or a moved closing arrives during the day, the associate updates the affected dates, recomputes the ratios and sends a revised report.

evidence.note: Margin calls arrive with short deadlines and peak in volatile markets. Share and times are the author's estimates.

exceptions.name: Cash breaks in opening balances
exceptions.description: Custodian and book-of-record cash disagree, for example an unbooked capital call payment or failed FX settlement, and must be explained before the forecast is built.

exceptions.name: Large unconfirmed private flows
exceptions.description: Closings, drawdowns or capital calls above the size threshold need date and amount confirmation from deal teams or funds operations, adding hours of waiting.

exceptions.name: Shortfall or early-warning breach
exceptions.description: The forecast shows a cash gap or the coverage ratio near an internal early-warning level; funding and balancing teams are engaged and a director may approve contingency actions.

exceptions.name: Large intraday flow
exceptions.description: A large unexpected margin call or accelerated capital call during the day triggers a reforecast and a revised report.

exceptions.name: Stressed market week
exceptions.description: In episodes like March 2020, margin calls jump, commercial paper may not roll and the team reforecasts several times a day; peer Canadian funds saw margin calls peak at about C$30 billion in one week.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: data ready about 03:00 to 05:00, report published late morning to early afternoon, later on days with funding actions or intraday reforecasts.

pain_points.description: Inputs arrive from many teams by email and report and are re-keyed into a spreadsheet model, so dates, signs and currencies are frequent error sources.

evidence.note: Spreadsheet-based forecasting is common; AFP notes dedicated software is more powerful.

pain_points.description: Private fund capital calls and closings have uncertain timing; the team waits for deal teams to confirm and still carries probability-weighted estimates.

evidence.note: Pacing and cash flow forecasts depend on uncertain private flows; notices reconcile earlier estimates.

pain_points.description: The forecast waits on upstream cash reconciliation and the collateral team's morning margin summary before it can be completed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common dependencies.

pain_points.description: Funding sources assumed in the buffer can disappear in stress, as US commercial paper did in March 2020, so capacity has to be confirmed rather than assumed.

evidence.note: Some Big Eight funds could not roll US commercial paper in March 2020.

assumptions: The process covers the daily forecast cycle only; monthly liquidity reporting to the Investment Risk Committee and annual calibration of stress assumptions are outside it.
Forecast horizons of 10 business days, three months and longer follow the 10-day and 6-month coverage horizons in the F2021 report; the exact model structure is not public.
Internal early-warning levels above the 1.0x Board limit are assumed; their values are not published. About 9% of days are assumed to need funding or cash-raising actions.
The commercial paper and repo capacity check is done by the CMF funding team, which the organisation file places in Financing, Collateral and Trading; a separate process issues the paper.
fte_on_process covers the daily cycle; the 18-person liquidity, leverage and collateral team also runs leverage management, collateral optimisation and plan transfers.
Loaded hourly costs come from the organisation file and include large incentive pay.
